label.type-only: The cycle never exists at runtime: at least one hop is removed when the file is compiled with the repo's own settings (an `import type`, an import whose bindings are only used as types or not at all while verbatimModuleSyntax is off, or a type-only re-export).
label.barrel-induced: The cycle exists at runtime only because a hop imports from a module that re-exports (a barrel, an index file or a package entry). If that import pointed at the module that declares the names, this cycle would not exist.
label.top-level-use: The cycle exists at runtime and some module on it reads a value imported from another module on it while it is being evaluated: a top-level statement or const initializer, a class `extends`, a static member, a decorator, or a top-level call that reaches the import. Depending on which module loads first, that read can throw a TDZ ReferenceError or see undefined.
label.late-use: The cycle exists at runtime and every value imported along it is only used inside functions or methods that run after all modules have loaded. Under ESM this is benign.
label.unclear: The code doesn't let you decide.

codebook.risk: For barrel-induced cycles, also say whether a value is read at module evaluation (top-level-use) or not (late-use).

rightFix.import-type: mark the import(s) `import type` (only for type-only cycles)
rightFix.import-direct: import from the declaring module instead of the re-exporting one
rightFix.extract-module: move the shared code into a new or lower module that both can import
rightFix.move-code: move a declaration from one file of the cycle to another
rightFix.lazy: defer the import (dynamic import() or a require inside a function)
rightFix.leave: leave it: the cycle is harmless and the change isn't worth it
